content.text: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/setting-up-nowpayments-digital-store-step-step-deployment-12|setting]] up a sovereign digital store is a four-step sequence that most creators overcomplicate by starting in the wrong order. Step one is the backend: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-webhook-driven-crypto-payment-fulfillment-explained-digital-22|Cloudflare Webhook-Driven]] Workers or Google Apps Script handles payment verification, order logging, and product delivery. Step two is the payment layer: NOWPayments connects your wallet addresses to the checkout flow — no KYC required from you or your buyer. Step three is the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages serves your store for free with no server management. Step four is testing: complete a real mainnet transaction, confirm the webhook fires, the order logs, and the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after step four passes cleanly should you promote the store. COREMERCH deploys the complete Edge Stack — Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/supabase-order-database-digital-stores-what-nobody-tells-4|COREMERCH guide to supabase]] plus NOWPayments — in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Stack 02 is designed to provide sovereignty over your digital commerce. Traditional payment processors can impose restrictions that limit your ability to sell. With Stack 02, you leverage Cloudflare’s infrastructure, which ensures high performance and reliability. This setup provides the required autonomy to process payments in over 300 cryptocurrencies, aligning perfectly with the needs of creators who face financial isolation in their regions.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Stack 02 — the Edge Commerce Stack — uses Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling, Supabase for order storage, Cloudflare R2 for product file delivery, and Resend for transactional email. The entire stack costs nothing per month up to significant volume thresholds — Cloudflare Workers provides 100,000 requests per day free, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage free, Cloudflare R2 provides 10GB storage and zero egress fees free, and Resend provides 3,000 emails per month free. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are configured during COREMERCH deployment.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, begin by configuring Cloudflare Workers to handle payment requests. Integrate NOWPayments to enable automatic payment processing. Connect your Supabase database to store orders and manage product inventory. Use Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file storage and delivery. This architecture ensures that your digital products are delivered instantly upon payment confirmation, enhancing customer satisfaction.
Own your entire digital commerce infrastructure with COREMERCH.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your infrastructure is set up, it’s time to go live. Test your store by processing a transaction using a test cryptocurrency. Ensure that the payment notification from NOWPayments is functioning correctly and that orders are recorded in Supabase. After validating the entire process, promote your store using your preferred marketing channels, leveraging social media and word of mouth to attract customers.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.

You can build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free by utilizing Stack 02 from COREMERCH, which offers a complete setup using Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase. This stack allows for seamless payment processing without relying on traditional financial platforms, enabling immediate access to your funds and data ownership.
Leverage Cloudflare's power for high-speed performance and security.

Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.
